newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Indonesia buys 13,000 tonnes olein from Malaysia.
newsitem.headline: Indonesia buys 13,000 tonnes olein from Malaysia.

text.p: Indonesia's state logistics agency BULOG said on Wednesday the country was taking delivery of 13,000 tonnes of palm olein imported from Malaysia, which would mark the final portion of a total 52,000 tonne delivery.

"Around 13,000 tonnes of olein from Malaysia will enter the country. This is part of a 52,000-tonne contract that we have signed. This is the last delivery," BULOG chief Beddu Amang told reporters. He did not give details on the timing of the imports.
On whether Indonesia, the world's second largest producer of crude palm oil after neighbouring Malaysia, will import more palm olein, Amang said: "We will see."
Palm olein is a crude palm oil-based cooking oil.

He confirmed that BULOG had commenced market operations on Tuesday to keep domestic palm olein prices stable ahead of the Moslem Ramadan fasting month that begins later this week and the ensuing Eid al-Fitr religious celebrations.
Indonesia has a policy of importing palm olein to stabilise the market when domestic demand rises.
He said BULOG would try to ensure local palm olein prices remained below 1,500 rupiah per kg. Prices on Wednesday were around 1,450-1,455 rupiah per kg in Jakarta, traders said.
Amang also said there was a need for Indonesia to maintain the export tax on crude palm oil and its products to ensure domestic prices did not track surges in international prices.
